title: Jesus Christ The Same Yesterday, Today, And Forever
summary: William Branham opens a revival meeting in Tallahassee, Florida, emphasizing that he is not a healer but that healing was already purchased at Calvary. He prays for the sick, demonstrating the Holy Spirit's ability to reveal hidden conditions and call people to faith in Christ.
themes: Jesus Christ the same yesterday, today, and forever
healing through faith in Christ's finished work
restoration of spiritual gifts in the last days

title: My Angel Shall Go Before Thee
summary: William Branham preaches on God's Angel leading His people, drawing from Exodus 23:20-23. He emphasizes that God has always had someone to work through, and that the same Holy Spirit who led Israel leads the church today. He encourages faith in divine healing, noting that prayer and belief in God's Word are powerful weapons against Satan.

title: Only Believe
summary: William Branham speaks on the importance of believing God's promises, using the example of Simeon who was promised he would not die before seeing the Christ. He encourages believers to trust in the redemptive blessings of Jesus and to exercise faith in the supernatural power of God.

title: All Things Are Possible To Them That Believe
summary: William Branham preaches on the power of belief, emphasizing that all things are possible to those who believe. He demonstrates the gift of discernment through prayer line healings, revealing specific conditions and personal details to individuals, and calls the congregation to accept their healing by faith.

title: Accept God's Gift
summary: William Branham preaches on accepting God's gift of salvation and healing through faith in Jesus Christ. He emphasizes that healing is already purchased at Calvary and must be received by confession and refusal of symptoms. He also discusses the Holy Spirit as a gift after believing.

title: Israel And The Church 1
summary: William Branham begins a five-night series on the Church, starting with Israel in Egypt. He emphasizes that salvation is by God's election and grace, not human works, and that the Old Testament is a shadow of the New. He teaches that God's covenant with Abraham is unconditional and fulfilled in Christ, and that the Holy Spirit is the seal of that covenant.
themes: Typology of Old and New Testaments
The Holy Spirit as the seal
The Church as the called-out people

title: Israel and the Church 2
summary: William Branham continues his study on the relationship between Israel and the Church, using Exodus as a type. He discusses election, justification, grace, and perfection through the patriarchs, and emphasizes the necessity of being born again by the Holy Spirit.

title: Israel and the Church 4
summary: William Branham continues his typological study of Israel's journey, comparing the Old Testament pilgrimage to the New Testament church. He focuses on the Israelites at Kadesh-barnea, where ten spies brought back an evil report of unbelief while Caleb and Joshua trusted God's promise. Branham applies this to the modern church, urging believers to have faith to enter the promised land of spiritual blessings.
themes: typology of Israel and the church
judgment beginning at the house of God
the sealing of the Holy Spirit
the contrast between true and false religion

title: Israel and the Church 5
summary: William Branham continues his series on Israel and the Church, drawing parallels between Joshua leading Israel into the Promised Land and the Church's journey today. He emphasizes the need to follow the Pillar of Fire (the Holy Spirit) rather than becoming trapped in organizations, and calls believers to put God first and cross their own Jordan.

title: The Cruelty of Sin, and the Penalty That It Cost to Rid Sin from Our Lives
summary: William Branham preaches on Good Friday about the cruelty of sin and the penalty required to remove it, using Isaiah 53 and the story of Cain and Abel to illustrate that only God's provided sacrifice—the blood of Christ—can atone for sin. He emphasizes the necessity of being born again and receiving the Holy Spirit, contrasting human efforts with God's way.

title: Go, Tell My Disciples
summary: In this Easter sermon, William Branham reflects on the resurrection of Jesus Christ as the foundational proof of His divinity. He contrasts the fear of death seen in unbelievers with the hope and victory believers have through Christ's resurrection, emphasizing that Jesus alone has power over death. Branham encourages believers to trust in the resurrection promise and to recognize Christ's presence in their lives.

title: Prayer
subtitle: 53-0405M
summary: A prayer delivered on Easter morning, reflecting on the resurrection of Christ and the hope of resurrection for believers. The speaker thanks God for Christ's victory over death and prays for forgiveness and faithfulness.

title: Witnesses
summary: William Branham preaches on the theme of being a witness for God, drawing from Acts 1:8. He emphasizes that a true witness must have a personal experience with God, not just secondhand knowledge. Using Old Testament examples like Noah, Shadrach, Meshach, Abednego, and David, he illustrates how God stands by those who courageously witness for Him, even through trials.

title: Prayer Line
summary: William Branham conducts a prayer line, praying for individuals with various ailments and encouraging faith in God's healing power. He emphasizes the prayer of faith and the importance of believing without doubt.

title: Jesus Christ the Same Yesterday, Today, and Forever
summary: William Branham speaks at the Bible Hour Tabernacle in Jonesboro, Arkansas, reflecting on his past meetings there and the faithfulness of God. He emphasizes that Jesus Christ is the same yesterday, today, and forever, and that divine healing is already provided at Calvary, requiring only faith to receive it. He illustrates this through biblical examples, including Jesus' encounter with Nathanael and the woman at the well, showing that Jesus only did what the Father showed Him.
themes: Jesus Christ the same yesterday, today, and forever

title: Expectations
summary: William Branham teaches on the character of Jesus Christ and how His Spirit works today, emphasizing that believers must expect God's promises to be fulfilled. He contrasts true faith with counterfeit spirituality, urging the congregation to claim their legal rights as children of God and refuse to accept Satan's afflictions.
themes: the Word of God as a seed

title: God Commissioning Moses
summary: William Branham preaches on God commissioning Moses and the importance of using what God has placed in your hand. He encourages believers to have faith and courage, using biblical examples like David and Goliath, Shamgar, and Samson to illustrate that God can use anyone who trusts Him.

title: The Pillar of Fire
summary: William Branham preaches on the Pillar of Fire that led Israel, identifying it as the Angel of the Covenant, Jesus Christ, who is the same yesterday, today, and forever. He shares personal testimony of a supernatural photograph taken in Houston, Texas, which he presents as scientific proof of the supernatural Being leading the Church today. He encourages believers to trust in God's leading and not to fear, as the same God who led Israel is present with them.

title: Testimony
summary: William Branham shares a testimony of God's healing power, recounting a vision of two Easter flowers that foretold the healing of a Finnish boy and the raising of another from the dead. He emphasizes faith in God's Word and the Holy Spirit's work today, urging believers to trust in Jesus Christ, the same yesterday, today, and forever.

title: We Have Found Him, Come And See
summary: William Branham preaches on the encounter between Philip and Nathanael, emphasizing that when one finds Jesus, they should invite others to 'come and see.' He discusses the importance of personal faith and confession in receiving healing, and demonstrates the gift of discernment by revealing specific conditions and sins to individuals in the congregation.
themes: The supernatural nature of the new birth

title: Speak to the Rock
summary: William Branham preaches on the resurrection and the importance of speaking to the Rock, Christ Jesus, for salvation and healing. He emphasizes that God's Word must be quickened by the Spirit and that faith comes by hearing and believing. The sermon includes a prayer line and demonstrations of the Holy Spirit's presence.

title: God's Provided Way
summary: William Branham preaches on God's provided way for salvation and healing, using the example of Moses lifting up the brass serpent in the wilderness. He emphasizes that Jesus Christ is the same yesterday, today, and forever, and that healing is already provided through the atonement. He encourages believers to trust in God's provision and to look to Christ for their needs.

title: Seeking After Jesus
summary: William Branham opens a revival meeting in Indiana, emphasizing that Jesus Christ is the same yesterday, today, and forever. He discusses divine healing, the importance of faith, and how Jesus' ministry is continued through the Holy Spirit in the church today. The sermon includes prayer for the sick and demonstrations of spiritual gifts.
themes: Jesus Christ the same yesterday, today, and forever
the role of the Holy Spirit in the church
rejection of Christ by religious leaders

title: Prayer Line
summary: William Branham conducts a prayer line, emphasizing faith and belief in God's power to heal. He explains that unbelief is sin and encourages attendees to come with faith.

title: Whatever He Says To You, Do It
summary: William Branham preaches on the importance of doing whatever Jesus says, using the wedding at Cana as a text. He emphasizes faith over hope, the reality of divine healing, and the presence of the Holy Spirit to confirm God's Word. The sermon includes prayer for the sick and several demonstrations of the gift of knowledge.

title: The Authority Of The Word
summary: William Branham preaches on the authority of God's Word and faith, using the centurion's story to illustrate that faith does not rely on symptoms but on God's spoken Word. He demonstrates the gift of discernment through prayer for the sick, calling out specific conditions and encouraging the congregation to accept their healing.

title: God Commissioning Moses
summary: William Branham preaches on God commissioning Moses and leading Israel by a pillar of fire, drawing parallels to the present-day ministry of the Holy Spirit. He shares a testimony of a supernatural photograph taken in Houston, Texas, as evidence of the same pillar of fire today, and emphasizes that Jesus Christ is the same yesterday, today, and forever.
themes: Jesus Christ the same yesterday, today, and forever

title: The Angel of the Lord
summary: William Branham preaches on the Angel of the Lord, emphasizing that Jesus Christ is the same yesterday, today, and forever. He shares testimonies of healings, including Congressman Upshaw and a young girl with tuberculosis, to demonstrate God's power and the importance of faith. Branham encourages believers to trust in God's Word and the Holy Spirit's work.

title: The Beginning of Jesus' Fame
summary: William Branham preaches on the unchanging nature of Jesus Christ, emphasizing that He is the same yesterday, today, and forever. He shares testimonies of divine healing, including the healing of Reverend Hall from cancer and the provision of a clinic for Dr. Sam Adair, demonstrating that God's power is still active today.

title: An Ensign
summary: William Branham preaches on the biblical typology of the brass serpent lifted by Moses as an ensign, connecting it to Christ's crucifixion as the ultimate ensign for salvation and healing. He emphasizes that looking to Jesus in faith brings both forgiveness and physical healing, and demonstrates the Spirit's discernment through a prayer line.

title: The Ministry of Christ
summary: William Branham preaches on the early ministry of Christ, using the raising of Lazarus as a central text. He emphasizes taking God at His Word, as exemplified by Mary's faith, and contrasts it with Zacharias's doubt. The sermon also touches on the need for a fresh daily experience with God.
themes: power of the name of Jesus

title: A Testimony
summary: William Branham shares a testimony of God's healing power, recounting a vision of a boy raised from the dead in Finland and a crippled girl healed. He emphasizes that Jesus Christ is the same yesterday, today, and forever, and that God confirms His Word through signs and wonders.
themes: Jesus Christ the same yesterday, today, and forever

title: Demonology, Physical Realm
summary: William Branham discusses the nature of demons and their role in sickness and disease, explaining that all sickness originates from Satan. He uses the analogy of a bear cub eating honey to illustrate the joy of the Holy Spirit, and delves into the spiritual and physical aspects of healing, emphasizing that faith is essential to maintain healing after a demon is cast out.
themes: the role of the Holy Spirit

title: At Thy Word
summary: William Branham opens a week of services, thanking God and the local officials. He preaches on taking God at His Word, using the story of Peter launching out into the deep at Jesus' command, and encourages believers to act on their faith.

title: Demonology, Religious Realm
summary: William Branham discusses demonology, explaining how demons can impersonate Christianity and work among believers. He shares personal experiences, including a vision about a future African crusade, and emphasizes the importance of testing spirits by Scripture and fruit.

title: MAKE THE VALLEY FULL OF DITCHES
summary: William Branham preaches on the need for faith and the moving of God's Spirit, using the story of Elisha and the kings of Israel and Judah. He emphasizes that God's presence is with those who respect Him and His Word, and encourages believers to seek a double portion of the Spirit.
themes: the double portion of the Spirit

title: Jesus Christ The Same Yesterday, Today, And Forever
summary: William Branham preaches on the unchanging nature of Jesus Christ, demonstrating through prayer and healing that Christ is the same yesterday, today, and forever. He calls the congregation to faith and repentance, leading many to salvation and the baptism of the Holy Spirit.

title: Palmerworm, Locust, Cankerworm, Caterpillar
summary: William Branham confesses that he has relied too much on the gift of discernment instead of simply praying for the sick as God commanded. He criticizes false healing practices and calls for unity among Pentecostal groups. He then reads from Joel 1:4 and discusses the spiritual condition of the church in the last days.

title: God's Provided Way
summary: William Branham shares testimonies of divine healing, including a woman healed by a prayed-over handkerchief and a demon-possessed woman delivered. He then preaches on God's provided way of salvation through Jesus Christ, using Old Testament types like Noah's ark and the Passover lamb to illustrate that God always provides a way of escape before judgment.

title: Earnestly Contending For The Faith That Was Once Delivered To The Saints
summary: William Branham preaches on Jude 3, urging believers to earnestly contend for the original faith delivered to the saints. He contrasts true faith with religious imitation, using Cain and Abel as examples of sincere but misguided worship versus God-ordained sacrifice. Branham emphasizes the need for a living, supernatural faith demonstrated by the power of the Holy Spirit.

title: I Perceive That Thou Art a Prophet
summary: William Branham speaks on the gifts of the Spirit, distinguishing between the gift of prophecy and the office of a prophet. He shares testimonies of healings and emphasizes that healing comes through personal faith in Christ. He also discusses the importance of financial integrity in ministry and the signs of the times.

title: Questions and Answers on Genesis
summary: William Branham answers questions about the creation of man in Genesis, explaining the difference between the spirit man created in God's image (Genesis 1:26-28) and the physical man formed from dust (Genesis 2:7). He discusses the pre-existence of souls, the origin of Eve, and where Cain got his wife, emphasizing that all races come from the same human stock.

title: THE TWENTIETH-CENTURY PROPHET
summary: William Branham recounts his early life, the supernatural experiences that marked his calling, and the development of his healing ministry. He describes visions, the appearance of the Angel of the Lord, and the fulfillment of prophecy in his work, including a resurrection. The sermon includes a prayer line demonstrating the gift of discerning of spirits and healing.

title: The Testimony of Jesus Christ
summary: William Branham preaches on the testimony of Jesus Christ, emphasizing that Jesus is the same yesterday, today, and forever, and that His works continue through the Church. He shares a testimony of a man healed from cancer through a divine vision and message, and then ministers to the sick, demonstrating the Spirit's discernment and power.

title: Why I Am a Holy-Roller
summary: William Branham explains why he identifies with the term 'holy-roller' by tracing the biblical lineage of true faith from Genesis onward. He contrasts the faith of Abel, Israel, and the early church—marked by signs and wonders—with mere fundamentalism that lacks divine vindication. Branham argues that the genuine church has always been a phenomenal people, persecuted by religious fundamentalists but vindicated by God through supernatural manifestations.

title: Come And See
subtitle: 53-0830E
summary: William Branham preaches on the importance of believing God's Word and the supernatural power of Christ. He reads John 1:44-51, focusing on Philip's invitation to Nathanael to 'come and see' Jesus. Branham then prays for the sick, demonstrating the gift of discernment and healing through the Holy Spirit.

title: God Talked to Moses
summary: William Branham preaches on the journey of Israel as a type of the Church, emphasizing the need to destroy spiritual enemies and claim God's promises. He contrasts the formalized churches with the moving of the Holy Spirit, and encourages believers to fight for their healing and baptism of the Holy Spirit.
themes: the Church as a called-out people
the Pillar of Fire as a type of the Holy Spirit

title: Lord, I Believe
summary: William Branham preaches on the healing of the blind man in John 9, emphasizing that faith must be accompanied by works. He prays for the sick, calling out specific ailments and encouraging believers to act on their faith.
themes: the power of the Holy Spirit

title: Testimony
summary: William Branham shares personal testimonies of God's grace and healing power, including a lesson about not judging others, a woman healed of a nose cancer, a demon-possessed woman delivered, and a blind girl healed in a parking lot. He emphasizes the importance of faith in Jesus Christ as the Healer.

title: Expectancy
summary: William Branham preaches on the theme of expectancy, using the biblical account of Simeon and Anna in the temple to illustrate how God leads those who are looking for Him. He emphasizes that God always has a witness and that the same Holy Spirit who led Simeon to see the Christ child leads people today to receive healing and salvation. The sermon includes a prayer line where Branham demonstrates the gift of discernment, revealing specific conditions and personal details to strangers as a sign of God's presence.

title: Healing (What Cancer Is)
summary: William Branham teaches on the nature of cancer as a spirit and explains the process of divine healing, emphasizing that healing is already provided at Calvary and must be received by faith. He also conducts a prayer line, demonstrating the gift of discernment and calling out specific conditions.

title: Faith Without Works Is Dead
summary: William Branham preaches on the necessity of faith accompanied by works, using James 2 as his text. He shares testimonies of healing and discernment, emphasizing that unconfessed sin blocks healing and that faith must be acted upon. The service includes prayer for the sick and a demonstration of the gift of discernment.

title: Believest Thou This?
summary: William Branham preaches on the resurrection of Lazarus from John 11, emphasizing faith in Jesus as the Resurrection and Life. He contrasts doubt with childlike faith, using examples like Mary's acceptance of Gabriel's message and the power of Jesus' name. He also shares personal anecdotes about missions, healing, and the need for genuine Christian love.

title: The Living Jesus Christ
summary: William Branham preaches on the living Jesus Christ, emphasizing His resurrection and continued work through the Holy Spirit. He shares testimonies of healings among Apache Indians and calls believers to have simple faith in God's Word.

title: Lord, Show Us The Father And It Sufficeth Us
summary: William Branham speaks on the longing to see God, using John 14:8 as a text. He explores seeing God in His universe, nature, and Word, and encourages believers to trust the Holy Spirit's leading over human organizations.

title: Healing Line
summary: William Branham conducts a healing service in Chicago, praying for the sick and demonstrating the gifts of the Spirit through words of knowledge and healing. He emphasizes faith in Jesus Christ as the Healer and encourages the congregation to believe and receive their healing.
themes: The power of the Holy Spirit
The Church as the body of Christ

title: Elijah
location: Louisville, Kentucky (Church Of The Open Door)
summary: William Branham uses the story of Elijah to call for spiritual preparation and unity among believers, emphasizing the need for heartfelt repentance and prayer to break the drought and bring revival. He warns that America's prosperity and moral decline mirror Israel's apostasy, urging individuals and churches to return to God.

title: Prayer Line
summary: William Branham conducts a prayer line, healing individuals with various ailments through the power of the Holy Spirit. He demonstrates discernment of illnesses and personal histories, rebukes demons, and encourages faith in Jesus Christ as the Healer.

title: Taking God at His Word
summary: William Branham preaches on the nature of faith as the sixth sense, contrasting it with the five physical senses. He emphasizes taking God at His Word, using the example of Peter letting down his net at Jesus' command, and encourages believers to trust in God's promises for healing and salvation.

title: Deep Calleth Unto The Deep
summary: William Branham preaches on the principle that a deep calling requires a deep to respond, using illustrations from nature, electricity, and healing. He explains the gift of visions and healing, demonstrating God's power through prayer and deliverance from deaf spirits and other ailments.

title: DO YOU NOW BELIEVE?
summary: William Branham preaches on the necessity of faith and the confirmation of God's Word through signs and wonders. He shares testimonies of healings and miracles, including a little boy raised from the dead in Finland and a woman healed of cancer, to encourage believers to trust in Christ as Healer and Saviour.

title: Jesus Christ The Same Yesterday, Today, And Forever
summary: William Branham demonstrates the gift of discernment and healing, showing that Jesus Christ is the same yesterday, today, and forever. He prays for individuals, revealing their conditions and bringing healing through faith. The sermon emphasizes that Jesus healed all believers 1900 years ago and that accepting this truth brings healing.
themes: Jesus Christ the same yesterday, today, and forever

title: Life Story
summary: William Branham shares his life story, from his impoverished childhood in Kentucky and Indiana to his calling by God. He recounts early hardships, his father's alcoholism, and his own determination to avoid sin, culminating in a divine encounter that set him apart for ministry.

title: Expectancy
summary: William Branham preaches on the theme of expectancy, using the biblical example of Simeon who waited for the Messiah. He encourages believers to expect God's intervention and healing, emphasizing that faith in God's Word brings results. The sermon includes prayer for the sick and demonstrations of spiritual gifts.

title: How the Angel Came to Me
summary: William Branham shares personal testimonies of divine healing and the ministry of the Angel of the Lord. He discusses the nature of faith, the baptism of the Holy Spirit, and the importance of obedience to God's word. The sermon includes accounts of healings and the role of visions in his ministry.

title: I Will Restore
summary: William Branham preaches on the restoration of the Church, using Joel 2:25 as a text. He contrasts true spiritual life with dead formalism, tracing the seed of the Church from Cain and Abel through Israel and the Reformation to the present day, emphasizing that God vindicates His people by signs and wonders.

title: Preparation
summary: William Branham speaks on the theme of divine preparation, explaining how God always prepares His people before major events. He contrasts man-made religion with God's provision, using examples from Eden, Noah, Moses, and Samson to illustrate that God's ways often seem foolish to human reason but are always effective. He calls for a genuine new birth and baptism of the Holy Spirit as the only true preparation for the last days.
themes: New birth and Holy Spirit baptism
God's ways seem foolish to man

title: Demonology
summary: William Branham discusses the reality of demons and spiritual warfare, contrasting true spiritual gifts with counterfeit spiritualism. He uses the example of a healing miracle featured in Reader's Digest to illustrate God's power, and warns against deception by demonic spirits that mimic the Holy Spirit.
themes: the Word of God as standard

title: Africa Trip Report
summary: William Branham shares his experiences from a missionary trip to Africa, recounting miraculous healings and visions. He emphasizes the importance of obeying God's direction over human plans, and describes how the Angel of the Lord appeared to confirm his ministry.

title: Speak to the Rock
summary: William Branham preaches on the journey of Israel from Egypt to the Promised Land as a type of the Christian experience, emphasizing the importance of staying under the blood of Christ and being filled with the Holy Spirit. He warns of coming judgment and urges repentance and a deep relationship with God.

title: A Greater Witness
summary: In this closing sermon of a revival in Owensboro, Kentucky, William Branham expresses gratitude to the congregation and emphasizes that healing comes through faith in Jesus Christ, not through any human gift. He reads from John 5:36 about the greater witness of Christ's works and calls the audience to accept their healing by faith, demonstrating God's presence through visions and prayer.
themes: The presence of the Holy Spirit
The role of prophets and gifts

title: Prayer Line
summary: William Branham conducts a prayer line, calling out various ailments and conditions through spiritual discernment. He emphasizes faith in Jesus Christ as the healer and encourages the congregation to believe for their healing.

title: Demonology
summary: William Branham shares his personal experiences with demonic spirits, including visions of demons leaving people and a dramatic confrontation with a possessed man in Portland. He discusses the importance of sincerity and faith in casting out devils, and recounts recent healings and the need for believers to cooperate fully with God.
themes: the role of the Holy Spirit

title: Brass Serpent
summary: William Branham preaches on the brass serpent in Numbers 21 as a type of Christ's crucifixion, emphasizing that looking to Jesus brings healing and salvation. He shares testimonies of healings and discusses the nature of God as Father, Son, and Holy Ghost.
themes: the nature of God as triune

title: The Resurrection of Lazarus
summary: William Branham speaks on the resurrection of Lazarus, emphasizing faith in God's power and the importance of believing in Jesus Christ as the resurrection and the life. He shares testimonies of healing and discusses the need for a genuine, Spirit-filled faith beyond mere church membership.

title: Prayer Line
summary: William Branham conducts a prayer line, calling out specific ailments and personal details of individuals in the congregation through the gift of discernment. He prays for healing and deliverance, encouraging faith in Jesus Christ. The sermon includes testimonies of healings and calls for repentance.

title: The Faith That Was Once Delivered To The Saints
summary: William Branham speaks on the need to earnestly contend for the faith once delivered to the saints. He contrasts the worship of Cain and Abel, emphasizing that true faith requires being born again, not just outward religion. He calls for a return to Holy Ghost revival and moral integrity.

title: Testimony
summary: William Branham shares a personal testimony about a debate on divine healing in Houston, Texas, where he and F.F. Bosworth defended the biblical basis of healing. He recounts how a supernatural light was photographed, providing scientific proof of God's presence. Branham also tells of healing miracles, including Florence Nightingale's granddaughter and King George VI.

title: Has The Lord Spoken Only To Moses?
summary: William Branham preaches on the power of the Gospel and the importance of believing in divine healing. He uses the story of Miriam and Aaron questioning Moses to illustrate the danger of speaking against God's servant. Branham shares testimonies of healings, including Congressman Upshaw, to demonstrate that God's power is still active today.
themes: The Gospel as power and demonstration

title: God's Provided Way
summary: William Branham preaches on God's provided way of escape through faith in His Word, using examples from Noah, Job, Moses, and the Passover. He emphasizes that salvation and healing come only through the Blood of Jesus Christ, and that believers must separate from the world and trust God's Word regardless of how foolish it may seem.
themes: the ark as a type of Christ

title: Testimony (Raising Dead Boy)
summary: William Branham shares a testimony about a vision he received of a little boy being raised from the dead, which he believed would come to pass. He encourages believers to claim God's promises by faith, using the example of Israel taking possession of the Promised Land. He also reflects on the importance of following the Spirit's leading rather than human reasoning.

title: At Thy Word
summary: William Branham shares personal testimonies of divine guidance and healing, emphasizing the importance of obeying the Holy Spirit's leading. He recounts stories of miraculous healings and visions, illustrating God's sovereignty and love for all people regardless of race or status.

title: The Resurrection
summary: William Branham preaches on the resurrection, emphasizing that believers will be restored to their youthful perfection. He contrasts the power of God's Word against Satan, discusses the sealing of the Holy Spirit, and calls for a return to old-fashioned Holy Ghost revival.

title: Life Story
summary: William Branham recounts the tragic loss of his father, brother, wife, and baby within a short period, leading him to contemplate suicide. He describes a vision of heaven where he meets his deceased daughter and wife, which renews his faith and commitment to God.

title: DO YOU NOW BELIEVE?
summary: William Branham speaks on the closing night of a small meeting, expressing gratitude and emphasizing the importance of sincerity and faith. He shares testimonies of healings and visions, including a story about Dr. Sam Adair's clinic and a woman's deliverance from nervousness through confession of sin. He concludes by reading John 5:33-36 and John 16:27-31, asking the congregation, 'Do you now believe?'
themes: the unchanging nature of Jesus Christ

title: The Inside Man
summary: William Branham speaks on the need for soul travail and unity among believers, emphasizing that sin is unbelief and that the Holy Spirit within believers enables them to do greater works. He uses the story of the brass serpent in Numbers 21 to illustrate faith and healing.

title: What Think Ye Of Christ?
summary: William Branham preaches on the identity of Jesus Christ as the Son of God, using biblical testimonies and personal anecdotes to affirm the virgin birth and Christ's divinity. He encourages believers to have faith in God's promises and to recognize the power of Christ's name.
